title: Throughput Safeguard Commitments and Contract Playbook
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Purpose: define a compact, auditable set of SLA definitions, error budget mechanics, and contract language that can be reused in Dedicated capacity agreements. This playbook balances predictable customer entitlements with operational flexibility (autoscale, burst windows, fallbacks). It is intended for PM + Legal + SRE review and to be used as canonical language in sales and contracts templates.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Clear SLA metric definitions that map to runtime telemetry (RPS, tokens/min, 99th latency)
2) Error budget formula documented with examples for monthly accounting
3) Contract clause drafts for notice, remediation, credits, and automatic fallbacks
4) Ops runbook for breach detection, credit calculation, and customer notifications
5) Legal review sign-off and one pilot customer contract insertion
success_metrics:
- Reduce contract negotiation time for throughput clauses by 30%
- Fewer post-signature SLA disputes (target: 0 in pilot cohort)
- Automated credit calculations match manual audits within 1%
- Detection to customer-notification median latency under 2 hours
contract_language_draft:
Summary clause: 'Redwood shall provide the Committed Throughput described in the Order Form, measured as tokens-per-minute (TPM) aggregated across the primary region(s). Committed Throughput guarantees apply on a 30-day rolling window with a monthly reconciliation. If Redwood fails to meet the Committed Throughput for a calendar month, the Customer will be entitled to Service Credits computed per the Error Budget Calculation below, subject to the Notice and Remediation procedures.'

Credit trigger: 'A credit is triggered when the realized throughput shortfall exceeds the monthly error budget threshold. Credits are capped at the monthly invoice for the Dedicated capacity. Credits are the Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for throughput degradations except for willful misconduct.'

Autoscale & fallback language: 'Redwood maintains autoscale policies and capacity pools which may be used to remediate temporary surges. Redwood will attempt automatic remediation before issuing credits. In cases where remediation requires incompatible model downscale or region failover, Redwood will provide advance notice where practicable and the Customer may elect to accept temporary model substitution or receive credits.'
error_budget_formula:
Definitions: Committed_TPM = contractual tokens-per-minute; Observed_TPM(t) = weighted median of per-second token rate for minute t across served capacity. Monthly Error Budget = sum_{t in month} max(0, Committed_TPM - Observed_TPM(t)).

Normalized Error Ratio = Monthly Error Budget / (Committed_TPM * minutes_in_month).

Credit tiers (example):
- Normalized Error Ratio < 0.01 => 0% credit
- 0.01 <= Ratio < 0.05 => 5% of monthly Dedicated fee
- 0.05 <= Ratio < 0.15 => 15% of monthly Dedicated fee
- Ratio >= 0.15 => 30% of monthly Dedicated fee (cap)

Notes: formula anchors on per-minute windows to avoid spiky artifacts and uses weighted median to be robust against metric outliers and client-side bursts.
measurement_method: Telemetry source: Redwood Console serving telemetry stream (per-VM token counters and aggregated per-az/region). Aggregation: 1-minute windows, compute per-customer aggregated Observed_TPM, then compute weighted median across the minute to smooth client jitter. Retention: raw 1-minute windows retained for 90 days for audits. Audit process: automated reconciliation job (monthly) that computes the error budget, stores a signed summary, and produces a human-readable reconciliation report for legal and customer support.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: Throughput burn rate anomaly (detected when 10-minute rolling Observed_TPM < 0.9 * Committed_TPM) -> Pager oncall (SRE) and notify account owner (AM)
Alert: Monthly reconciliation scheduled and results ready -> PM + Legal distribution list receives report
Dashboard: Per-customer throughput corridor with committed line, observed median, and 95th percentile shading
SLO heartbeat: daily computed health score; if health score < 0.95 for three consecutive days open incident and run mitigation checklist
escalation_playbook: 1) Detection: automated job raises alert -> 2) Triage (SRE oncall) collects traces, region/host health, autoscaler logs -> 3) If remediation possible (capacity reclaim, autoscale event), SRE triggers automated remediation and reports to AM; track time-to-remediate. If not, 4) Notify customer within 2 hours with status, expected remediation ETA, and mitigation options (e.g., model variant or region failover). 5) After 24 hours of degraded service start credit pre-approval flow with Legal and Billing to prepare provisional credit. 6) Post-incident, run RCA and attach remediation plan; adjust error budget/thresholds if systemic. 7) If repeated breaches exceed contract thresholds, trigger executive review and contractual remediation ladder (discounts, termination rights outlined in contract).
timeline_updates: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Khatri: initial draft of formula and credit tiers posted; asked SRE for feasibility review
2026-02-20 - Marcus Rivera (SRE): flagged risk with per-minute aggregation on bursty ingress; recommended weighted median approach
2026-02-23 - Legal review (Sarah O'Neill): requested explicit cap language and sole-remedy clause; asked for examples of credit math for $/month sizes
2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: accepted weighted median telemetry approach; added retention and audit requirements
2026-03-09 - Customer Success (Priya Patel): requested inclusion of a 48-hour escalation SLA for enterprise onboarding customers; added to playbook
stakeholder_feedback: SRE: prefer conservative tiers and operational runbook; Legal: wants clear allocation of discovery/audit windows; Sales: wants deterministic, easy-to-communicate credit bands for negotiation. Customer Success: prefers proactive remediation and customer-visible failover options over credits where possible.
notes_for_legal:
- Ensure 'sole and exclusive remedy' language is balanced against enterprise negotiations (some customers will request liability carveouts).
- Define precise notice windows for customers to submit disputes (30 days after reconciliation).
- Include auditability clause specifying Redwood's reconciliation job output is the primary source of truth but customer may request replay within 90 days subject to confidentiality and cost recovery.
- Consider alternate tier language that ties credits to measurable business impact (e.g., unsuccessful committed requests) for large enterprise customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal review with SRE/Legal/Finance by 2026-03-15. 2) Pilot the clause with two committed customers starting April billing cycle (opt-in). 3) Collect pilot results for 60 days, adjust tiers and monitoring thresholds. 4) Publish contract template and internal sales guidance. 5) Bake reconciliation automation into billing pipeline (engineering EPIC).
open_questions: Should we include latency-based credits in addition to throughput?
How to handle multi-region customers whose traffic splits vary unpredictably?
What is the acceptable audit cost and how to charge for customer-initiated audits?
final_notes: This playbook prioritizes clear, measurable commitments and operational steps to avoid ambiguous interpretations. The goal is to provide customers with predictable recourse while preserving Redwood's ability to run autoscale/fallback policies that keep services available. Legal and SRE sign-off required before general availability.
